title: Mexico Customs System Outage Halts World Trade Bridge Cargo for Hours
excerpt: Mexico's customs clearance system went down nationwide Wednesday morning, halting commercial crossings at the World Trade Bridge for about three hours and backing up trucks for miles — westbound Loop 20 was closed to traffic heading into Mexico until the system came back around 2:30 p.m.
content:
Mexico’s customs clearance system went down nationwide on Wednesday morning, halting commercial crossings at the World Trade Bridge for about three hours and backing up trucks for miles on the Laredo side, according to reports from both sides of the border.

The system that clears goods through Mexican customs failed around 11 a.m. Wednesday, Nov. 25, according to Noreste Digital. For about three hours, commercial exchange at the World Trade Bridge customs house was suspended because of repeated failures in the clearance system, which is run from Mexico City.

The Nuevo Laredo cargo carriers association told its members in bulletin No. 047/2026, sent at 12:15 p.m., that the central customs system was down and that both imports and exports were halted, with updates to follow. El Mañana de Nuevo Laredo flagged the outage as breaking news, citing a report from Laredo police.

Texas Department of Transportation cameras at FM 1472 and Killam and at Loop 20 and FM 1472 showed miles-long lines of tractor-trailers queued on the approach roads and ramps to the bridge.

The Laredo Police Department said an export system was down throughout Mexico and warned of traffic backups at the World Trade Bridge, according to KGNS. Police closed westbound Loop 20 to traffic heading into Mexico. Around 2:30 p.m., police said the system was back up.

Drivers and carriers said the failure landed at the worst moment, just as cargo volume climbs into the December holiday season, and they called for measures to keep it from becoming the pattern for the month. One operator told Noreste Digital that efforts to speed up import and export crossings keep stalling, and that even with room to add more inspection modules, the crossing keeps running short-handed.

Sources: Noreste Digital — “¡Varó la carga!; piden choferes evitar los “nudos” decembrinos”, Nov. 25, 2026, https://norestedigital.net/index.php/2026/11/25/varo-la-carga-piden-choferes-evitar-los-nudos-decembrinos/; KGNS — “Export system outage prompts Loop 20 closure, police say”, Nov. 25, 2026, https://laredonews.org/news/export-system-outage-prompts-loop-20-closure-police-say; El Mañana de Nuevo Laredo, Nov. 25, 2026; Asociación de Transportistas de Carga de Nuevo Laredo bulletin No. 047/2026, Nov. 25, 2026
